title: Version orchestration workbench: pinning, staging lanes, and perf snapshot explorer
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a unified "version orchestration workbench" in the Redwood Console that lets teams discover model versions, compare performance profiles, create scoped pins (route/team/account), stage rollouts via lanes, and publish performance profiles with an auditable changelog.
context_and_problem_statement: Customers pin model versions to achieve deterministic behavior, but current console flows scatter pinning, perf-viewing, and rollout controls across multiple screens. This leads to accidental global pins, lack of visibility into expected perf/cost trade-offs, and difficulty safely rolling a new version into production. We need a single workbench that makes the composition of routing, pin scope, rollout percentage, and performance expectations explicit and reviewable.
goals: Single-screen workflow to search, compare, and pin model versions
Make performance profile deltas and cost estimates visible before pinning
Support scoped pinning: route-level, project/team-level, and account-level
Allow staged rollouts with lanes (canary, ramp, full) and rollback triggers
Publish and sign performance profiles with short changelog and verification checklist
Provide audit trail and exportable JSON for infra automation
acceptance_criteria: Users can open workbench from a model’s Console page or from a route's settings
Comparative view shows latency/throughput/cost/quality metrics for selected versions and highlights statistically significant deltas
Pin modal supports selecting scope (route, team, account), and optional rollout lanes with percentage and time windows
Publish profile flow requires author, summary, and optional verification links; publishes an immutable snapshot visible in perf explorer
Audit trail entry created for every pin/publish action with user, timestamp, diff, and optional PR link
Rollout UI exposes automatic rollback conditions (error rate > X, latency > Y) with a preview of affected routes
design_notes: Introduce a left rail for version selection + filter (architecture, quantization, compute tier)
Center panel for side-by-side perf profiles: baseline (current pinned) vs candidate
Right rail for pin configuration: scope, rollout lanes, schedule, preflight checks
Inline delta badges (green/red) with confidence level and sample size
Compact timeline control for staging lanes with drag-to-adjust percentages and duration
Preview button that simulates routing outcomes (percentages applied) and shows estimated cost delta
Accessibility: keyboard-first controls for lane adjustment, high-contrast delta labels, aria summaries for audit entries
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Keep preflight checks optional to avoid blocking fast iterations, but show strong warnings when checks are skipped
We considered embedding a full statistical hypothesis tester; instead surface key signals (p95 latency, 99th, token cost, quality score) with links to deeper analysis to reduce cognitive load
Expose rollout automation but keep manual override as default to avoid unexpected customer traffic shifts
Decided not to allow cross-account pins in UI; require API/infra tools for multi-account orchestration for security reasons
engineering_notes: Depends on ENG-2140 (perf-profile immutable snapshots API) and ENG-2198 (scoped pin API)
Backend must return pre-computed perf deltas for selected time windows to avoid expensive client joins
We should surface whether a model variant supports KV cache/quantization compatibility (ENG-2250 planned)
usability_research: Remote 1:1 sessions with 6 platform engineers; observed confusion around scope selection leading to accidental global pins
Key insight: users want an explicit summary card that says 'This action will affect X routes and Y users'
Prototype A (lane slider) had 83% task success; Prototype B (percentage input) had 58% success — prefer slider + numeric input combo
review_feedback: PM: Add cost delta card with 7-day projected spend impact (requested by PM L. Hwang)
Engineering: Flag offline-only fields that require backend feature flags (ENG-2140)
Security: Add audit export option and require SSO author for publish actions (Slack thread #security-publish)
Design: Simplify left rail filters to primary selectors (architecture, quantized/float, region) — defer advanced filters to expansion panel
open_questions: Should publish require sign-off from a separate reviewer for high-impact pins? (proposal: require reviewer if customer_impact is high)
How to represent uncertainty for small sample sizes in perf deltas? (confidence band vs explicit 'insufficient data')
Do we surface projected token cost per 1M tokens or per-request average? both?
next_steps: Validate high-fidelity mocks in next week’s research sessions (schedule with 4 platform teams)
Sync with ENG-2140 owner to finalize API contract and perf delta payloads (target: 2026-03-12)
Prepare PRD for release manager including rollback automation knobs and metric thresholds
Create accessibility checklist and keyboard-only QA plan

risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Users accidentally perform global pins — Mitigation: prominent scoping summary and a force-confirm for global scope
Risk: Perf deltas misinterpreted due to small sample sizes — Mitigation: show sample size and gray out low-confidence deltas
Risk: Backend API latency causing UI flakiness — Mitigation: optimistic UI with clear in-flight indicators and retry guidance
final_notes: This ticket is the design anchor for the next console release. Keep scope minimal for MVP: selection, compare, pin with scope, stage lanes, publish snapshot. Defer multi-account orchestration and advanced statistical tests to follow-ups.
